text.p: These are the highlights in the Bosnian press on Thursday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- International High Representative to Bosnia, Carlos Westendorp, said he hopes the donors' conference will be held on July 22 or 23.

- Memorandum with International Monetary Fund on financial and economic policy from July 1996 to June 1997 will be adopted soon. A crucial last condition for donors' conference is an agreement on design of Bosnian currency, according to Westendorp.
- Final decision on currency design will be made by Bosnia's presidency, says Kasim Omicevic, central bank vice-governor.
- Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) office in Sarajevo says that 2,471,722 voters have registered for the forthcoming municipal elections in September.
- Kris Janowski, spokesman for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), says recent political events have overshadowed a key element of the peace agreement - return of refugees.
- U.S. diplomat Richard Kauzlarich has been nominated by Washington for ambassador's post to Bosnia.
- In a discussion on distribution of diplomatic posts, Moslem side insists on opening of at least 67 ambassadorial posts.
- Deputy foreign minister, Dragan Bozanic, a Serb, says an agreement has been reached on 37 ambassador posts.
- European Union officials said they would suspend aid to the Bosnian Serb entity due to the failure of its leaders to hand over indicted war criminals.

- Federation Prime Minister Edhem Bicakcic rejected recent criticism by trade union president over price hikes for public services. Bicakcic said the government was responsible for the price increases for power and postal services, but the remainder were under the supervision of cantonal governments.

- U.S. President Bill Clinton, speaking at a NATO summit in Madrid, expanded the mandate of NATO officers in Bosnia, saying if they judge a risk is acceptable, they should arrest indicted war criminals. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
